findings.claim: CG-R3-001 residual: _build_snapshot try/except catches only RuntimeError; subprocess.TimeoutExpired (raised by subprocess.run when git process exceeds _RESOURCE_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30s) is not a RuntimeError subclass and escapes the isolation block, crashing the entire snapshot build and taking all 11 resource URIs offline — the same blast-radius as the pre-fr3 bug, triggered by a different mechanism.
findings.evidence: resources.py:564-583: except clause is 'except RuntimeError as error'. Python exception hierarchy: subprocess.TimeoutExpired → subprocess.SubprocessError → Exception (not RuntimeError). When _read_committed_text (line 565) calls _git_stdout (line 104), which calls subprocess.run(..., timeout=_RESOURCE_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) (line 105), a git process that does not complete within 30 seconds raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired. This is not caught by 'except RuntimeError'; it propagates through _build_snapshot uncaught, through snapshot() (line 474) which holds _snapshot_lock but does not update self._snapshot, then re-raises. All callers (read_static, read_rule, read_waiver, read_finding, read_decision) share the same snapshot() call path and become unavailable. On next request, snapshot() retries from scratch: _head_commit() (another subprocess call) + _build_snapshot() → hits _read_committed_text again → TimeoutExpired again. Under concurrent 021H HTTP load, each in-flight request triggers one subprocess call per timeout cycle. test_signing_keys_outage.py covers only RuntimeError paths (malformed two-current and empty keyring); no test exercises a git subprocess timeout scenario to verify degraded behavior.
findings.impact: A transient git filesystem hang (slow NFS, repo lock contention, OOM-killed git process) lasting >30s on the signing-keys read causes complete MCP resource unavailability for all 11 URIs for the duration of the hang, defeating the isolation invariant established by fr3. The invariant 'signing-keys failure → isolated to scp://security/signing-keys only' does not hold for the TimeoutExpired path.
findings.mitigation: In resources.py:581 change 'except RuntimeError as error' to 'except (RuntimeError, OSError) as error'. subprocess.TimeoutExpired inherits from subprocess.SubprocessError which inherits from OSError in Python 3.3+; this catches both parse failures and git subprocess errors (timeout, missing executable, permission denied) in a single clause with no behavioral change to the existing RuntimeError path. Add a third test in test_signing_keys_outage.py that patches subprocess.run to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired and asserts: (a) catalog.snapshot() does not raise; (b) read_static('scp://security/signing-keys')['error'] is not None; (c) read_static('scp://decisions')['key_id'] is None.

R1 SB-MAJ-001 mitigation: '021F adopter guide must contain an explicit warning that scp://security/signing-keys is transport-trust-dependent and must be backed by the committed-file fallback.' No plan amendment found in §4 021F row.
findings.impact: 021F reviewer has no visible obligation to verify the warning; SB-MAJ-001 attack surface (adopter trusting MCP-delivered key without committed-file cross-check) can re-open silently at 021F ship.
findings.mitigation: Add named tracked-forward item to WP-SCP-021 §4 021F row: 'signing-keys-adopter-warning: adopter guide must state scp://security/signing-keys is transport-trust-dependent; hooks must cross-check current_key.public_key against committed docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub before accepting any verification result.' No code change required.

findings.claim: CG-R3-007 carry-forward: test_resource_schemas.py reads schemas via CWD-relative Path('schemas/scp_mcp') — fails when pytest is invoked from any directory other than the project root.
findings.evidence: R3 evidence: test_resource_schemas.py:15 schema_root = Path('schemas/scp_mcp'); not re-verified in R4 but no commit in git log suggests amendment. CWD-relative path unchanged.

structured_review.fixpoint_note: 3 of 4 R3 completeness MAJ blockers fully closed: CG-R3-002 (trust_model text corrected, test assertion updated), CG-R3-003 (§13 Resolution column added with substantive closure notes for all nine unknowns), CG-R3-004 (instructions field accurately enumerates 7 tools and 11 URI types, cross-checked against tools.py register_tools and resources.py STATIC+TEMPLATE URIs). CG-R3-001 (blast-radius isolation) is 90% closed: the RuntimeError degradation path is correctly isolated by try/except RuntimeError in _build_snapshot:581, outage tests cover it, and all non-signing-keys resources remain operational on parse failure. Residual gap: subprocess.TimeoutExpired (raised when git exceeds 30s timeout) is not a RuntimeError subclass and escapes the clause, reproducing the original blast-radius scenario via a different trigger. This is new blocker CG-R4-001. Fix is one-line: change 'except RuntimeError' to 'except (RuntimeError, OSError)'. Minimum scope for fr4: (1) resources.py:581 except clause broadened to include OSError; (2) one new test in test_signing_keys_outage.py patching subprocess.run to raise TimeoutExpired and asserting degraded envelope + cross-resource key_id=None. Once CG-R4-001 is closed, completeness lens has no new MAJ blockers; MIN/nit carry-forwards (CG-R3-005 pyproject deps, CG-R3-006 021F warning, CG-R3-007 CWD path, CG-R4-002 propose anti-spam note) do not block fixpoint declaration.

r3_closure_verification.evidence: resources.py:560-625 _build_snapshot: lines 564-583 wrap _read_committed_text + _parse_signing_keys + empty-key guard + missing-current-key guard in try/except RuntimeError. On exception, RESOURCE_LOGGER.error fires at ERROR level and signing_keys_body = _degraded_signing_keys_payload(str(error)) is assigned, returning {current_key: None, current_key_sha256: None, prior_keys: [], keys: [], error: <message>, trust_model: ...}. current_key_id remains None. _build_snapshot continues: registry, domain-map, waivers, decisions, findings, status all build under key_id=None. signing_keys_resource = _resource_envelope(signing_keys_body, key_id=None). scp://security/signing-keys returns the error envelope; scp://decisions et al. are operational. test_signing_keys_outage.py covers: (1) duplicate current=true markers → RuntimeError('multiple current signing keys declared') → signing_keys['error'] populated, signing_keys['current_key'] is None, signing_keys['key_id'] is None, all STATIC_RESOURCE_URIS + rule/waiver/finding/decision per-ID reads have key_id=None; (2) empty keyring → RuntimeError('contains no ssh-ed25519 key entries') → same degraded envelope; log confirms 'degrading MCP resource snapshot: signing-keys unavailable'. The blast-radius isolation required by R3 mitigation is confirmed for all RuntimeError paths. Residual for subprocess.TimeoutExpired elevated to new finding CG-R4-001.

resources.py:154-168 _signing_keys_trust_model(): adopter_requirement = 'Adopters MUST verify current_key.public_key against an out-of-band trust anchor such as the committed docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub file at a known git SHA or an operator-distributed public key hash. Resource-only cross-checks are insufficient; current_key_sha256 is informational, not authoritative.' The phrase 'or a pinned sha256' is absent; current_key_sha256 is explicitly labeled informational, not authoritative; out-of-band committed-file requirement is primary. verification_roots[1] reads 'operator-distributed public key hash' — no sha256 self-reference. test_signing_keys.py:28-29 asserts 'out-of-band trust anchor' in payload['trust_model']['adopter_requirement'] and 'or a pinned sha256' not in payload['trust_model']['adopter_requirement']. Both assertions verify the R3 mitigation text is live and regression-protected.
